product_family: Gradescope: AI-assisted grading and assessment platform for higher education, supporting paper-based exams, homework, programming assignments, bubble sheets, and code autograders. Acquired by Turnitin in 2018.

certifications.proof_quote: Vendor domain (gradescope.com/privacy): 'over 160 controls aligned to the SOC2 criteria were designed for Turnitin and audited for effectiveness. Turnitin successfully satisfied 100% of the controls audited.' Corroborated by Turnitin self-attestation to Microsoft (updated Oct 23 2025): 'Which SOC 2 certification did you achieve? type2 | Most recent SOC2 certification date: 2024-11-26'

privacy.ai_training_note: AI training posture for Gradescope is unclear. The Terms of Service grant Turnitin a 'royalty-free, sublicensable, transferable, perpetual, irrevocable, non-exclusive, worldwide license' to use User Content, with a carve-out: Educational Records may be used 'solely on an aggregated, de-identified basis and will not share such information with third parties.' Gradescope's AI-assisted grading feature groups similar student answers using AI, which is limited to Institutional plan. No explicit statement on whether student submissions train underlying AI/ML models is present in Gradescope-specific documentation. The Microsoft attestation confirms 'Does the app perform automated decision making, including profiling that could have a legal effect or similar impact? No.' No explicit AI training opt-out is documented for Gradescope.
privacy.data_region: United States, Germany, Australia (per Microsoft attestation). Privacy policy notes Gradescope data can be processed in Europe, Canada, Australia, or United States depending on institution preference, except handwritten formula recognition which requires US processing.

security.name: Encryption in transit
security.value: SSL/TLS encryption stated in privacy policy. Microsoft attestation confirms TLS 1.1 or higher supported.

security.name: Encryption at rest
security.value: Privacy policy references 'robust physical, digital, and procedural safeguards including SSL encryption, redundant servers and data centers.' At-rest encryption not explicitly confirmed for Gradescope data.

security.name: Data hosting
security.value: AWS (Amazon Web Services) confirmed as cloud provider per Microsoft attestation. PaaS model.

security.name: Penetration testing
security.value: Annual penetration testing confirmed ('Do you perform annual penetration testing on the app? Yes').

security.name: Vulnerability scanning
security.value: Quarterly vulnerability scanning confirmed ('Do you conduct quarterly vulnerability scanning on your app and the infrastructure that supports it? Yes').

security.name: Multi-factor authentication (MFA)
security.value: MFA enabled for code repositories, DNS management, and credentials per Microsoft attestation.

security.name: Intrusion Detection/Prevention
security.value: IDPS deployed at network perimeter ('Do you have Intrusion Detection and Prevention (IDPS) software deployed at the perimeter of the network boundary supporting your app? Yes').

security.name: Incident response
security.value: Formal security incident response process documented. Breach notification to supervisory authorities and individuals within 72 hours confirmed.

security.name: Disaster recovery
security.value: Documented disaster recovery plan including backup and restore strategy confirmed.

security.name: SSO / LMS integration
security.value: LTI 1.3 and SSO available on Institutional plan. Microsoft Entra ID integration supported.

security.name: Student Privacy Pledge
security.value: Turnitin took the Student Privacy Pledge (FPF/SIIA), committing not to sell student data or use it for targeted advertising.

products.name: Gradescope Basic
products.data_scope: Student submissions (PDFs, instructor-uploaded or student-uploaded), rubrics, grades, comments, personal data (name, email, institution)
products.notes: Free plan for individual instructors. Includes rubric management, PDF uploads, assignment statistics, regrade requests. No AI features. No LMS integration.

products.name: Gradescope Institutional
products.data_scope: Same as Basic plus code submissions, bubble sheet scans, handwritten formula images (US-processed), collaborative grading data
products.notes: Custom pricing per institution, per-student. Adds AI-assisted grading, answer grouping, anonymous grading, LMS integration, SSO, admin dashboard, code similarity detection, and dedicated onboarding. AI features include AI-powered roster matching and AI-powered answer grouping.

compare.pricing_model: Free basic tier (Gradescope Basic for individual instructors); Institutional plan is custom-quoted per university at an estimated $1-$3 per student per course based on third-party sources. No public pricing page for Institutional.
compare.data_residency: US, EU (Germany), Australia. Institutional clients may have some regional preference options per privacy policy, but handwritten formula recognition always requires US processing.

flags: The scope of the SOC 2 Type 2 certification (dated 2024-11-26) is ambiguous: the primary evidence comes from Turnitin's self-attestation for the Microsoft Teams integration, not Gradescope specifically. The privacy policy on the vendor's own domain confirms Turnitin's SOC 2 audit but does not specify the Type or scope. Buyers should request the SOC 2 report directly to confirm Gradescope is in scope.
The Cyber Essentials certification was issued in November 2019 and requires annual renewal, but no evidence of renewal after 2019 was found; the certification may have lapsed.

The AI training posture is unclear: the Terms of Service grant Turnitin a broad perpetual license over User Content, with Educational Records carved out to an 'aggregated, de-identified basis only.' However, no explicit Gradescope-specific policy states whether student submissions are used to train AI models, a gap for institutions uploading sensitive student work.

Stanford Internet Observatory research found that Gradescope previously sent student PII (names, emails, grades, instructor comments) to FullStory via embedded analytics scripts. Remediation and the current status of third-party analytics data sharing are not confirmed in current documentation.

Turnitin's 2018 press materials referenced EU-US Privacy Shield certification, a framework that was invalidated by Schrems II in July 2020. The current privacy policy correctly uses Standard Contractual Clauses (Model Contractual Clauses), so the outdated reference is historical, not a current compliance gap.
